what_worked: Revenue concentration slide (7) attempts a real analytical point with a chart and interpretive callout.
fix_next: Replace decorative illustrations with actual data charts; cite specific numbers from the dataset with sample sizes and limitations.
verdict: Generic startup advice dressed as data analysis; almost no verifiable dataset findings.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: '3-5x Higher Revenue' B2B vs B2C — actual median multiples are ~2.3x, not 3-5x. Slide 7: '17.5% Total conversion rate' appears from nowhere in the dataset. Slide 7: bar chart values (40/35/18/7) are round fabricated numbers not matching actual top-10 share of 49.6%. Slide 8: '2-3x Better Retention' — no retention data exists in the dataset. Slide 8: '40%+ Revenue Predictability' — no such metric in the data.

evidence.insight: Every major claim (B2B wins, subscriptions beat one-time, geographic arbitrage) is a generic startup truism. No category medians, provider breakdowns (Stripe/RevenueCat/Dodo), TLD analysis, or anonymity revenue share explored. No original finding surfaced from the actual dataset.
evidence.narrative: Loose arc from opportunity to action, but reads as a listicle of startup platitudes. The 'three paths' conclusion on slide 9 could apply to any startup dataset or none at all. No thesis is built from specific data discoveries.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 poses a question but never defines scope (30-day revenue snapshots, self-reported data). 241 missing countries, 274 missing categories, 216 zero-revenue rows never acknowledged. Audience implied but dataset constraints completely hidden from reader.
evidence.accuracy: Multiple invented statistics: 3-5x B2B advantage overstates actual ~2.3x median multiple; 2-3x retention and 40%+ predictability reference metrics absent from the dataset; 17.5% conversion rate is unexplained and unsourced; slide 7 bar chart uses suspiciously round numbers that don't match actual concentration figures (top-10 share is 49.6%).
evidence.visual: Consistent warm palette and bold typography provide cohesion. However, only one chart across 9 slides (slide 7), and it uses fabricated-looking round numbers. Every slide features decorative clip-art (robot hand, conveyor belt, crowd, rocket, globe) that adds zero analytical value. Repetitive three-column card layout on slides 3, 5, 8, 9 is template-driven.
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive: decorative stock illustrations on every slide, inflated consulting language ('brutally concentrated,' 'revenue treadmill,' 'life-changing revenue,' 'the data doesn't lie'), fabricated statistics presented without sourcing, and identical three-column card layouts repeated across multiple slides. Content could describe any startup ecosystem without modification.
